newsitem.title: UK: IPE crude sinks as expiring NYMEX gasoline sold.
newsitem.headline: IPE crude sinks as expiring NYMEX gasoline sold.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were sharply lower on Thursday, shedding over 45 cents on the back of selling of the expiring NYMEX August gasoline contract.
By 1426 GMT front month Brent was 470 cents lower at $18.50, well below Wednesday's eight week $19 high.
"The market wasn't as strong as expected when New York opened," one broker said. "There has been some strong liquidation of the expiring August gasoline contract."
News from the U.N. also helped the fall, brokers said.

The United Nations was expected to approve Iraq's aid-distribution plan, the final hurdle to a resumption of Iraqi exports under the UN food-for-oil deal, by the weekend, well-placed sources at the organisation said.
"The UN official's comment has helped the fall along," one broker said.
Front-month NYMEX unleaded gasoline and heating oil contracts expire on Thursday.
NYMEX crude was 60 cents lower at $19.70 a barrel while unleaded gasoline was 2.7 cents lower at 67.20 cents a gallon.
September Brent had closed 38 cents higher on Wednesday at $18.97 a barrel, just three cents off the day's 8-week $19 high.
